tree.notes: Frog has no external tail, so only 5 leaves: head + 4 limbs. Spine simplified to a root splitting into a short 'hip' segment (toward rear, holding both hind-leg roots) and a longer 'shoulder' segment (toward front, holding head and both fore-leg roots), matching the side-view body outline from x=0 (rump) to x=24 (snout) with a fairly flat back (y=7-8 throughout). Each limb was split into three anatomical segments (upper/lower + terminal) since only the overall limb envelope is directly visible in the side view: front leg = shoulder_*->elbow_*->hand_*, hind leg = hip_*->knee_*->foot_*. Side view gives the x/y (forward/height) component of each joint; the front and top views (leg spread width) were used to infer the z (lateral) component and to justify giving left/right legs mirrored, fully independent chains (each rooted at the shared spine node 'shoulder' or 'hip', never merging distally). All vertical descents (hip->knee->ankle->foot and shoulder->elbow->wrist->hand) were converted to NEGATIVE dy per the flip rule, since these joints move downward on the screen toward the ground line (y≈19-20) from the back line (y≈7-8). Lengths are taken from the straight-line pixel/grid distances between consecutive side-view joint readings, rounded to the nearest integer.

tree.notes: Starfish has radial symmetry with 5 rays (arms) and no distinct head/tail, so leaves = the 5 arm tips only. The mesh is essentially flat (thin in Z, confirmed by the front and top views showing only the disc thickness in Z), so all arm directions are encoded in the XY plane (dz=0). Individual arm tip readings from the side view were asymmetric (lengths ~11.5-13) due to mid-pose/rendering variance, but per the proportion-not-pose rule all five arms were authored with equal integer length (12), the average of the readings, while preserving each arm's individual direction vector so the stick figure still fans out correctly. No internal joints were added within each arm since starfish rays are unjointed soft appendages (unlike vertebrate limbs), so each arm is a single segment from the central disc (root, length 0) to its tip. Two arm pairs (upper-left/upper-right and lower-left/lower-right) were marked as symmetric leaf pairs; the top arm is unpaired (the fifth, axial ray).

Flippers, dorsal fin, and tail fluke are modeled as single-segment appendages (no internal joints) since they are stiff fin/fluke structures rather than jointed limbs - this segmentation (no thigh/knee-style sub-joints) is an inferred simplification per protocol note #8. Left/right flipper chains are fully independent, each parented to the shared 'chest' spine node, per the two-full-limbs rule.
